newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market calm as holiday mood kicks in.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market calm as holiday mood kicks in.

text.p: Dutch rates were unchanged on Wednesday in an extremely sluggish money market.
"It's obvious the holiday season is upon us," a dealer said.
Most money market rates have remained flat over the last couple of weeks, except for call money. Call money eased on an ample allocation under last week's special advances pact.
Call money slipped below 3.00 percent last week after the announcement of the pact. It was bid for at 2.88 to 2.93 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
Other money market deposits and Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) were also unchanged.
Dealers said the holiday season, combined with the absence of a clear direction, had braked market activity.
"If you don't know where you're going, you're better off doing nothing at all rather than risk losing your money," one dealer said.
Another said a tighter allocation under Friday's new special advances pact might boost call money slightly, but he did not expect the Dutch central bank to adjust the rate.

Last week, Rabobank and ING Barings said the central bank might raise the special advances rate 10 basis points soon because of recent guilder ($5.04) weakness against the German mark and Germany's repo remaining at 3.00 percent.
Dealers were not surprised to find the Finance Ministry's Agency had bought back DTCs last week.
It bought back 500 million guilders of DTCs maturing this month and 33 million guilders of paper maturing in December.
"It was obvious they had too much money in cash, so getting out of this month's DTCs early seems a logical thing," one dealer said.
Some said the Finance Ministry's Agent also put out call money and very short-term deposits.
"But now the (Agency's) cash balance (at the Dutch central bank) is back to zero," he said.
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark, trading at 112.571 per 100 marks versus 112.575.
